### Replace src/router.tsx with Convex client setup

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/tanstack-start

Creates a ConvexClient and ConvexQueryClient, wires in a ConvexProvider, and integrates with React Query and the router. Requires VITE_CONVEX_URL environment variable.

```tsx
import { createRouter } from "@tanstack/react-router";

import { QueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";

import { setupRouterSsrQueryIntegration } from "@tanstack/react-router-ssr-query";

import { ConvexQueryClient } from "@convex-dev/react-query";

import { ConvexProvider } from "convex/react";

import { routeTree } from "./routeTree.gen";



export function getRouter() {

  const CONVEX_URL = (import.meta as any).env.VITE_CONVEX_URL!;

  if (!CONVEX_URL) {

    console.error("missing envar VITE_CONVEX_URL");

  }

  const convexQueryClient = new ConvexQueryClient(CONVEX_URL);



  const queryClient: QueryClient = new QueryClient({

    defaultOptions: {

      queries: {

        queryKeyHashFn: convexQueryClient.hashFn(),

        queryFn: convexQueryClient.queryFn(),

      },

    },

  });

  convexQueryClient.connect(queryClient);



  const router = createRouter({

    routeTree,

    defaultPreload: "intent",

    context: { queryClient },

    scrollRestoration: true,

    Wrap: ({ children }) => (

      <ConvexProvider client={convexQueryClient.convexClient}>

        {children}

      </ConvexProvider>

    ),

  });

  setupRouterSsrQueryIntegration({ router, queryClient });



  return router;
}
```

### Create a script to load data from Convex

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/python

Creates main.py that uses ConvexClient to query and subscribe to the "tasks:get" API. The subscribe loop runs forever until interrupted.

```python
import os
from convex import ConvexClient
from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv(".env.local")
CONVEX_URL = os.getenv("CONVEX_URL")
# or you can hardcode your deployment URL instead
# CONVEX_URL = "https://happy-otter-123.convex.cloud"
client = ConvexClient(CONVEX_URL)
print(client.query("tasks:get"))
for tasks in client.subscribe("tasks:get"):
    print(tasks)
    # this loop lasts forever, ctrl-c to exit it
```

--------------------------------

### Connect Rust app to Convex backend

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/rust

Creates a ConvexClient in src/main.rs, loads the deployment URL from environment variables, and queries the 'tasks:get' API.

```rust
use std::{
    collections::BTreeMap,
    env,
};
use convex::ConvexClient;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    dotenvy::from_filename(".env.local").ok();
    dotenvy::dotenv().ok();
    let deployment_url = env::var("CONVEX_URL").unwrap();
    let mut client = ConvexClient::new(&deployment_url).await.unwrap();
    let result = client.query("tasks:get", BTreeMap::new()).await.unwrap();
    println!("{result:#?}");
}
```

export const { signOut, refreshSession, isAuthenticated } = auth;



export const { startSignInWithApple, completeSignInWithApple } = setupApple(

  auth,

  {

    component: components.authApple,

    allowedRedirectOrigins: [

      "https://app.example.com",

      "http://localhost:5173",

    ],

  },

).attachUserCallbacks({ createUser: internal.users.createUserApple });
```

const app = defineApp();

app.use(agent);



export default app;

### Update src/router.tsx to wire Convex and React Query

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/tanstack-start

Creates a ConvexClient and ConvexQueryClient, wires them into a QueryClient and ConvexProvider, and sets up SSR query integration.

```tsx
import { createRouter } from "@tanstack/react-router";import { QueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";import { setupRouterSsrQueryIntegration } from "@tanstack/react-router-ssr-query";import { ConvexQueryClient } from "@convex-dev/react-query";import { ConvexProvider } from "convex/react";import { routeTree } from "./routeTree.gen";export function getRouter() {  const CONVEX_URL = (import.meta as any).env.VITE_CONVEX_URL!;  if (!CONVEX_URL) {    console.error("missing envar VITE_CONVEX_URL");  }  const convexQueryClient = new ConvexQueryClient(CONVEX_URL);  const queryClient: QueryClient = new QueryClient({    defaultOptions: {      queries: {        queryKeyHashFn: convexQueryClient.hashFn(),        queryFn: convexQueryClient.queryFn(),      },    },  });  convexQueryClient.connect(queryClient);  const router = createRouter({    routeTree,    defaultPreload: "intent",    context: { queryClient },    scrollRestoration: true,    Wrap: ({ children }) => (      <ConvexProvider client={convexQueryClient.convexClient}>        {children}      </ConvexProvider>    ),  });  setupRouterSsrQueryIntegration({ router, queryClient });  return router;}
```

### Stream deltas asynchronously with DeltaStreamer and streamText

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/agents/streaming

Uses the DeltaStreamer class to save deltas to the database while streaming with the AI SDK's streamText function. Requires a threadId from the Agent component and a distinct order for each stream. The example uses the Convex AI Gateway; see Getting Started for installation and requirements.

```typescript
import { components } from "./_generated/api";

import { type ActionCtx } from "./_generated/server";

import { DeltaStreamer, compressUIMessageChunks } from "@convex-dev/agent";

import { streamText } from "ai";

import { convexGateway } from "@convex-dev/ai-sdk-provider";



async function stream(ctx: ActionCtx, threadId: string, order: number) {

  const streamer = new DeltaStreamer(

    components.agent,

    ctx,

    {

      throttleMs: 100,

      onAsyncAbort: async () => console.error("Aborted asynchronously"),

      // This will collapse multiple tiny deltas into one if they're being sent

      // in quick succession.

      compress: compressUIMessageChunks,

      abortSignal: undefined,

    },

    {

      threadId,

      format: "UIMessageChunk",

      order,

      stepOrder: 0,

      userId: undefined,

    },

  );

  // Do the normal streaming with the AI SDK

  const response = streamText({

    model: convexGateway("openai/gpt-5-mini"),

    prompt: "Tell me a joke",

    abortSignal: streamer.abortController.signal,

    onError: (error) => {

      console.error(error);

      streamer.fail(errorToString(error.error));

    },

  });



  // We could await here if we wanted to wait for the stream to finish,

  // but instead we have it process asynchronously so we can return a streaming

  // http Response.

  void streamer.consumeStream(response.toUIMessageStream());



  return {

    // e.g. to do `response.toTextStreamResponse()` for HTTP streaming.

    response,

    // We don't need this on the client, but with it we can have some clients

    // selectively not stream down deltas when they're using HTTP streaming

    // already.

    streamId: await streamer.getStreamId(),

  };

}
```

### Update src/routes/__root.tsx to add QueryClient to router context

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/tanstack-start

Adds a QueryClient to the router context so React Query is usable anywhere in the TanStack Start site.

```tsx
import { QueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";import { createRootRouteWithContext } from "@tanstack/react-router";import { Outlet, Scripts, HeadContent } from "@tanstack/react-router";import * as React from "react";export const Route = createRootRouteWithContext<{  queryClient: QueryClient;}>()({  head: () => ({    meta: [      {        charSet: "utf-8",      },      {        name: "viewport",        content: "width=device-width, initial-scale=1",      },      {        title: "TanStack Start Starter",      },    ],  }),  component: RootComponent,});function RootComponent() {  return (    <RootDocument>      <Outlet />    </RootDocument>  );}function RootDocument({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {  return (    <html>      <head>        <HeadContent />      </head>      <body>        {children}        <Scripts />      </body>    </html>  );}
```

--------------------------------

### Add the script to your webpage

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/script-tag

Creates an `index.html` file that uses the Convex browser bundle and a `ConvexClient` to subscribe to updates on the `tasks:get` query. The `CONVEX_URL` placeholder must be replaced with the development environment URL from `.env.local`. The client logs task text each time the `tasks` table is modified.

```html
<!doctype html><script src="https://unpkg.com/convex@1.3.1/dist/browser.bundle.js"></script><script>  const CONVEX_URL = "CONVEX_URL_GOES_HERE";  const client = new convex.ConvexClient(CONVEX_URL);  client.onUpdate("tasks:get", {}, (tasks) =>    console.log(tasks.map((task) => task.text)),  );</script>
```

--------------------------------

### Display tasks in src/routes/index.tsx

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/tanstack-start

Replace the file with this content. The useSuspenseQuery hook renders the api.tasks.get query result on the server initially, then updates live in the browser.

```typescript
import { convexQuery } from "@convex-dev/react-query";

import { useSuspenseQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";

import { createFileRoute } from "@tanstack/react-router";

import { api } from "../../convex/_generated/api";



export const Route = createFileRoute("/")({

  component: Home,

});



function Home() {

  const { data } = useSuspenseQuery(convexQuery(api.tasks.get, {}));



  return (

    <div>

      {data.map(({ _id, text }) => (

        <div key={_id}>{text}</div>

      ))}

    </div>

  );
}
```

### Tasks composable to display data

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/android

Replace the template composables with a Tasks composable that subscribes to the tasks:get query and displays each task in a LazyColumn.

```kotlin
@Composablefun Tasks(modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {    val tasks: Result<List<Task>> by client.subscribe<List<Task>>("tasks:get")        .collectAsState(Result.success(listOf()))    LazyColumn(        modifier = modifier    ) {        items(tasks.getOrElse { emptyList() }) { task ->            Text(text = "Text: ${task.text}, Completed?: ${task.isCompleted}")        }    }}
```

### Setup GitHub sign-in with Convex Auth

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/convex-auth-api/methods/github/server

Complete setup for GitHub sign-in. Requires installing the component in convex.config.ts under httpPrefix: "/oauth/github" and registering <site-url>/oauth/github/callback as the redirect URI with GitHub. The httpPrefix alone determines the callback URL.

```typescript
const auth = setupConvexAuth({ component: components.auth });

export const { signOut, refreshSession, isAuthenticated } = auth;



export const { startSignInWithGithub, completeSignInWithGithub } = setupGithub(

  auth,

  {

    component: components.authGithub,

    allowedRedirectOrigins: [

      "https://app.example.com",

      "http://localhost:5173",

    ],

  },

).attachUserCallbacks({ createUser: internal.users.createUserGithub });
```

--------------------------------

### Define HTTP routes in a component's http.ts

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/components/authoring

Components can define their own HTTP routes using an http.ts file. The app that installs the component chooses where these routes are accessible by specifying an httpPrefix. This example defines a GET route at '/hello' that returns a simple response.

```typescript
import { httpRouter } from "convex/server";

import { httpAction } from "./_generated/server";



const http = httpRouter();



http.route({

  path: "/hello",

  method: "GET",

  handler: httpAction(async () => {

    return new Response("hello from component", { status: 200 });

  }),

});



export default http;
```

--------------------------------

### setupConvex(url, options?)

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/svelte/reactivity

Initializes the Convex client and stores it in Svelte context. Call once in a root layout. Returns a ConvexClient instance.

```APIDOC
## setupConvex(url, options?)

### Description
Initializes the Convex client and stores it in Svelte context. Call once in a root layout. Returns a ConvexClient instance.

### Parameters
- **url** (string) - Required - The Convex deployment URL.
- **options** (object) - Optional - Additional options for the client.

### Returns
- **ConvexClient** - The initialized Convex client.
```

### Manual fetch with getServiceToken

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/ai-gateway/setup

Use fetch to call the AI Gateway HTTP API without an SDK. Mint a token with getServiceToken("ai-gateway") and send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>. The example posts to https://ai-gateway.convex.dev/v1/chat/completions with model openai/gpt-4o-mini.

```typescript
import { action } from "./_generated/server";

import { v } from "convex/values";

import { getServiceToken } from "convex/server";



export const chat = action({

  args: { prompt: v.string() },

  handler: async (ctx, { prompt }) => {

    const token = await getServiceToken("ai-gateway");

    const response = await fetch(

      "https://ai-gateway.convex.dev/v1/chat/completions",

      {

        method: "POST",

        headers: {

          Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,

          "Content-Type": "application/json",

        },

        body: JSON.stringify({

          model: "openai/gpt-4o-mini",

          messages: [{ role: "user", content: prompt }],

        }),

      },

    );

    return await response.json();

  },

});
```

### Start async video generation with experimental_startVideo

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/ai-gateway/images-and-videos

Use experimental_startVideo when the action should return before the video is ready. Create a job in your database and pass its ID as requestId so the callback handler can look up the job. For local development, omit webhookUrl; callbacks require a cloud deployment's HTTPS convex.site URL. maxRetries: 0 prevents automatic submission retries, and keep webhookSecret private.

```typescript
import { experimental_startVideo as startVideo } from "ai";

import { convexGateway } from "@convex-dev/ai-sdk-provider";



async function startJob(requestId: string) {

  const modelId = "google/veo-3.1";

  const started = await startVideo({

    model: convexGateway.videoModel(modelId),

    prompt: "A camera pan across a mountain lake",

    duration: 8,

    webhookUrl: `${process.env.CONVEX_SITE_URL}/video-complete?requestId=${requestId}`,

    maxRetries: 0,

  });



  return {

    modelId,

    operation: started.operation,

    inferenceId: started.providerMetadata?.convexGateway?.inferenceId,

    webhookSecret: started.providerMetadata?.convexGateway?.webhookSecret,

  };

}
```

--------------------------------

### Client configuration with root route and auth setup

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/auth/authkit/add-to-app

Configures the TanStack Start root route with Convex and WorkOS AuthKit, including SSR auth token setup and document shell.

```TypeScript
import { HeadContent, Outlet, Scripts, createRootRouteWithContext } from '@tanstack/react-router';

import { getAuth } from '@workos/authkit-tanstack-react-start';

import appCssUrl from '../app.css?url';

import type { QueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

import type { ConvexReactClient } from 'convex/react';

import type { ConvexQueryClient } from '@convex-dev/react-query';



export const Route = createRootRouteWithContext<{
  queryClient: QueryClient;
  convexClient: ConvexReactClient;
  convexQueryClient: ConvexQueryClient<ConvexReactClient>;
}>()({
  head: () => ({
    meta: [
      {
        charSet: 'utf-8',
      },
      {
        name: 'viewport',
        content: 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1',
      },
      {
        title: 'Convex + TanStack Start + WorkOS AuthKit',
      },
    ],
    links: [
      { rel: 'stylesheet', href: appCssUrl },
      { rel: 'icon', href: '/convex.svg' },
    ],
  }),
  component: RootComponent,
  notFoundComponent: () => <div>Not Found</div>,
  beforeLoad: async (ctx) => {
    const auth = await getAuth();

    // During SSR only (the only time serverHttpClient exists),
    // set the WorkOS auth token to make HTTP queries with.
    if (auth.user) {
      ctx.context.convexQueryClient.serverHttpClient?.setAuth(auth.accessToken);
    }

    return { user: auth.user };
  },
});

function RootComponent() {
  return (
    <RootDocument>
      <Outlet />
    </RootDocument>
  );
}

function RootDocument({ children }: Readonly<{ children: ReactNode }>) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <HeadContent />
      </head>
      <body>
        {children}
        <Scripts />
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

### Display data with useQuery in src/routes/+page.svelte

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/svelte

Uses useQuery to subscribe to the api.tasks.get API function and renders the tasks with loading and error states.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">	import { useQuery } from 'convex-svelte';	import { api } from '../convex/_generated/api.js';
	const query = useQuery(api.tasks.get, {});
</script>
{#if query.isLoading}
	Loading...
{:else if query.error}
	failed to load: {query.error.toString()}
{:else}
	<ul>
		{#each query.data as task}
			<li>
				{task.isCompleted ? '☑' : '☐'}
				<span>{task.text}</span>
				<span>assigned by {task.assigner}</span>
			</li>
		{/each}
	</ul>
{/if}
```

### Basic usage: helloWorld action

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/agents/getting-started

Define a Convex action that creates a thread and generates text with the agent. If you get type errors about components.agent, ensure you've run npx convex dev to generate code for the component.

```typescript
import { action } from "./_generated/server";

import { createThread } from "@convex-dev/agent";

import { v } from "convex/values";



export const helloWorld = action({

  args: { city: v.string() },

  handler: async (ctx, { city }) => {

    const threadId = await createThread(ctx, components.agent);

    const prompt = `What is the weather in ${city}?`;

    const result = await agent.generateText(ctx, { threadId }, { prompt });

    return result.text;

  },

});
```

### Display data with useQuery in pages/index.js

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/nextjs/pages-router/quickstart

Use the useQuery hook to fetch from api.tasks.get and render the task text. The tasks are mapped to div elements with the _id as key.

```javascript
import { useQuery } from "convex/react";

import { api } from "../convex/_generated/api";



export default function Home() {

  const tasks = useQuery(api.tasks.get);

  return (

    <main className="flex min-h-screen flex-col items-center p-24">

      {tasks?.map(({ _id, text }) => (

        <div key={_id}>{text}</div>

      ))}

    </main>

  );
}
```

### Configure ConvexProviderWithAuth0 in src/main.tsx

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/auth/auth0

Replace ConvexProvider with Auth0Provider wrapping ConvexProviderWithAuth0. Add domain and clientId props to Auth0Provider.

```tsx
import React from "react";

import ReactDOM from "react-dom/client";

import App from "./App";

import "./index.css";

import { ConvexReactClient } from "convex/react";

import { ConvexProviderWithAuth0 } from "convex/react-auth0";

import { Auth0Provider } from "@auth0/auth0-react";



const convex = new ConvexReactClient(import.meta.env.VITE_CONVEX_URL as string);



ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(

  <React.StrictMode>

    <Auth0Provider

      domain="your-domain.us.auth0.com"

      clientId="yourclientid"

      authorizationParams={{

        redirect_uri: window.location.origin,

      }}

      useRefreshTokens={true}

      cacheLocation="localstorage"

    >

      <ConvexProviderWithAuth0 client={convex}>

        <App />

      </ConvexProviderWithAuth0>

    </Auth0Provider>

  </React.StrictMode>,

);
```

### Logout button with useAuth0

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/auth/auth0

Redirects the user to the Auth0 logout endpoint. Uses the useAuth0 hook and specifies returnTo as the current origin.

```TypeScript
import { useAuth0 } from "@auth0/auth0-react";



export default function LogoutButton() {

  const { logout } = useAuth0();

  return (

    <button

      onClick={() =>

        logout({ logoutParams: { returnTo: window.location.origin } })

      }

    >

      Log out

    </button>

  );

}

### setupConvexAuthServer(config)

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/convex-auth-api/ssr

Configures the auth handlers once and returns an object with routes to mount. The returned object includes `convexProxyHandler` for sign-in, `refreshHandler` for refreshing sessions, and `signOutHandler` for signing out.

```APIDOC
## setupConvexAuthServer(config)

### Description
Configures the auth handlers once and returns an object with routes to mount. The returned object includes `convexProxyHandler` for sign-in, `refreshHandler` for refreshing sessions, and `signOutHandler` for signing out.

### Parameters
- `config` (ConvexAuthServerConfig) - Required - Configuration for the auth server.

### Returns
- `convexProxyHandler` (RequestHandler) - The sign-in route. Mount it once at a static path, and every function in `signIn` is reachable from the normal client hook of its method.
- `refreshHandler` (RequestHandler) - The refresh handler.
- `signOutHandler` (RequestHandler) - The sign-out handler.

### Example
```ts
// auth.ts
export const auth = setupConvexAuthServer({
  convexUrl: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL!,
  refreshSession: api.auth.refreshSession,
  signOut: api.auth.signOut,
  signIn: [
    api.auth.signInWithUsernamePassword,
    api.auth.signUpWithUsernamePassword,
  ],
  cookieOptions: { secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production" },
});

// app/auth/signin/route.ts
import { auth } from "@/auth"; // the result of `setupConvexAuthServer`
export const POST = auth.convexProxyHandler;
```
```

import { AuthConfig } from "convex/server";



export default {

  providers: [

    {

      domain: "your-domain.us.auth0.com",

      applicationID: "yourclientid",

    },

  ]

} satisfies AuthConfig;
```

### Stream text with streamText and convexGateway

```typescript
import { streamText } from "ai";

import { convexGateway } from "@convex-dev/ai-sdk-provider";



const result = streamText({

  model: convexGateway("openai/gpt-4o-mini"),

  prompt,

});

for await (const chunk of result.textStream) {

  console.log(chunk);

}

### React component for GitHub OAuth sign-in and sign-out

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/auth/convex-auth/methods/oauth

Uses useSignInWithGithub from @convex-dev/auth/methods/github/react to start GitHub OAuth, and useOauth to handle errors after redirect. Handles start errors and flow errors with exhaustive switches on error codes. Requires Convex auth setup and the api.auth reference.

```tsx
import { type ReactNode, useState } from "react";

import { useConvexAuth, useQuery } from "convex/react";

import { useAuthActions } from "@convex-dev/auth/react";

import {

  useOauth,

  useSignInWithGithub,

} from "@convex-dev/auth/methods/github/react";

import { api } from "../convex/_generated/api";



/**

 * A failure to start comes back from the sign-in call, and a failure after the

 * redirect back shows up in `useOauth`'s `flowError`. Each is handled with an

 * exhaustive switch on its code.

 */

function SignedOut(): ReactNode {

  const { signIn } = useSignInWithGithub(api.auth);

  const { flowError } = useOauth();

  const [startError, setStartError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  return (

    <>

      <h1>Sign in</h1>

      <p>Continue with your GitHub account</p>

      {flowError !== null && (

        <p role="alert">

          <strong>

            {(() => {

              switch (flowError.error) {

                case "ACCESS_DENIED":

                  return "Sign-in was cancelled.";

                case "EXPIRED":

                  return "That sign-in took too long. Please try again.";

                case "INVALID_FLOW":

                  return "This sign-in can't be completed here. Please try again.";

                case "OTHER_ERROR":

                  // The details are on `cause` if you want to log them.

                  return "Something went wrong during sign-in. Please try again.";

                default:

                  flowError satisfies never;

                  return `Unknown error: ${JSON.stringify(flowError)}`;

              }

            })()}

          </strong>

        </p>

      )}

      {startError !== null && (

        <p role="alert">

          <strong>{startError}</strong>

        </p>

      )}

      <button

        type="button"

        onClick={async () => {

          setStartError(null);

          const result = await signIn();

          if (result.status === "redirect") return;

          switch (result.userError.error) {

            case "OTHER_ERROR":

              // The flow couldn't start, e.g. the deployment was

              // unreachable. The original error is on `cause` if you want

              // to log or inspect it.

              console.error(

                "GitHub sign-in failed to start:",

                result.userError.cause,

              );

              setStartError("Couldn't start GitHub sign-in. Please try again.");

              return;

            default:

              result.userError.error satisfies never;

              console.error(

                "GitHub sign-in failed to start:",

                result.userError,

              );

              setStartError("Couldn't start GitHub sign-in. Please try again.");

          }

        }}

      >

        Continue with GitHub

      </button>

    </>

  );

}



function SignedIn(): ReactNode {

  const { signOut } = useAuthActions();

  const user = useQuery(api.users.getCurrentUser);

  return (

    <>

      <h1>Signed in</h1>

      <p>{user?.id ?? "…"}</p>

      <button type="button" onClick={() => void signOut()}>

        Sign out

      </button>

    </>

  );

}



export default function App(): ReactNode {

  const { isLoading, isAuthenticated } = useConvexAuth();

  return (

    <main>

      {isLoading && <p>Signing you in…</p>}

      {!isLoading && isAuthenticated && <SignedIn />}

      {!isLoading && !isAuthenticated && <SignedOut />}

    </main>

  );

}
```

### Display tasks with useQuery in app/page.tsx

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/nextjs

Uses the useQuery hook to fetch from api.tasks.get and renders the task text.

```typescript
"use client";import Image from "next/image";import { useQuery } from "convex/react";import { api } from "../convex/_generated/api";export default function Home() {  const tasks = useQuery(api.tasks.get);  return (    <main className="flex min-h-screen flex-col items-center justify-between p-24">      {tasks?.map(({ _id, text }) => (        <div key={_id}>{text}</div>      ))}    </main>  );}
```

--------------------------------

### Connect app to Convex backend in pages/_app.js

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/nextjs/pages-router/quickstart

Create a ConvexReactClient and pass it to a ConvexProvider wrapping your app. Uses the NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL environment variable.

```javascript
import "@/styles/globals.css";

import { ConvexProvider, ConvexReactClient } from "convex/react";



const convex = new ConvexReactClient(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL);



export default function App({ Component, pageProps }) {

  return (

    <ConvexProvider client={convex}>

      <Component {...pageProps} />

    </ConvexProvider>

  );
}
```

--------------------------------

### Configure authentication provider in convex/auth.config.ts

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/auth/convex-auth/getting-started

Tells your deployment to accept the access tokens of Convex Auth. Your deployment signs the access tokens with its own key, so you do not have secrets to configure.

```typescript
import type { AuthConfig } from "convex/server";

import { convexAuthProvider } from "@convex-dev/auth/server";



export default {

  providers: [convexAuthProvider()],

} satisfies AuthConfig;
```

### initConvex(url, options?)

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/svelte/sveltekit-server-rendering

Creates the ConvexClient singleton early. Only needed for the convexLoad setup.

```APIDOC
## initConvex(url, options?)

### Description
Creates the ConvexClient singleton early. Only needed for the convexLoad setup.

### Parameters
- **url** (string) - Required - The deployment URL.
- **options** (InitConvexOptions) - Optional - Options including queryCache settings.
```

### Access Auth0 user in React with useAuth0 hook

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/auth/auth0

Use the useAuth0 hook from @auth0/auth0-react to access the authenticated user's information, such as their name, in a React component.

```tsx
import { useAuth0 } from "@auth0/auth0-react";



export default function Badge() {

  const { user } = useAuth0();

  return <span>Logged in as {user.name}</span>;

}
```

--------------------------------

### Check auth state with useConvexAuth

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/auth/auth0

Checks whether the user is logged in or not. The useConvexAuth hook ensures the browser has fetched the auth token needed for authenticated requests.

```TypeScript
import { useConvexAuth } from "convex/react";



function App() {

  const { isLoading, isAuthenticated } = useConvexAuth();



  return (

    <div className="App">

      {isAuthenticated ? "Logged in" : "Logged out or still loading"}

    </div>

  );

}
```

### SwiftUI ViewModel observing ConvexClient subscription

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/swift

Adapts the colors:get example to a ViewModel: ObservableObject class. The View observes the ViewModel as a @StateObject and rebuilds when it changes, so the View no longer directly fetches data.

```swift
import SwiftUIclass ViewModel: ObservableObject {  @Published var colors: [String] = []  init() {    convex.subscribe(to: "colors:get")      .replaceError(with: [])      .receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)      .assign(to: &$colors)  }}struct ContentView: View {  @StateObject var viewModel = ViewModel()  var body: some View {    List {      ForEach(viewModel.colors, id: \.self) { color in        Text(color)      }    }  }}
```

--------------------------------

### setupConvexAuthServer usage example

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/convex-auth-api/ssr

Example of configuring the auth handlers with setupConvexAuthServer in auth.ts. It sets the convexUrl, refreshSession, signOut, signIn, and cookieOptions. The signIn array lists the methods that will be served by the sign-in route.

```typescript
// auth.ts

export const auth = setupConvexAuthServer({

  convexUrl: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL!,

  refreshSession: api.auth.refreshSession,

  signOut: api.auth.signOut,

  signIn: [

    api.auth.signInWithUsernamePassword,

    api.auth.signUpWithUsernamePassword,

  ],

  cookieOptions: { secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production" },

});
```

### Display query results in src/routes/index.tsx

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/tanstack-start

Replaces `src/routes/index.tsx` to render the `api.tasks.get` query result. The `useSuspenseQuery` hook with `convexQuery` renders the data on the server initially, then updates live in the browser.

```typescript
import { convexQuery } from "@convex-dev/react-query";import { useSuspenseQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";import { createFileRoute } from "@tanstack/react-router";import { api } from "../../convex/_generated/api";export const Route = createFileRoute("/")({  component: Home,});function Home() {  const { data } = useSuspenseQuery(convexQuery(api.tasks.get, {}));  return (    <div>      {data.map(({ _id, text }) => (        <div key={_id}>{text}</div>      ))}    </div>  );}
```

### Manual scaffold sequence for a new Convex project

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/ai/using-conductor

Run these commands in order to scaffold a new Convex project before pointing Conductor at it. The sequence creates a new app, enters its directory, and installs Convex AI files.

```bash
npm create convex@latest my-app

cd my-app

npx convex ai-files install
```

### Initialize convexTest with schema

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/testing/convex-test

Call convexTest(schema) at the start of each test to enable schema validation and correct typing for t.run. The returned object is stored in t and provides methods for exercising Convex functions.

```TypeScript
import { convexTest } from "convex-test";

import { test } from "vitest";

import schema from "./schema";



test("some behavior", async () => {

  const t = convexTest(schema);

  // use `t`...

});
```

npx @convex-dev/bundle-analyzer summary
```

### Infer TypeScript type from validator

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/api/modules/values

Use the Infer type to extract a TypeScript type from a validator. The example defines an object schema with v.object and v.string, then uses Infer<typeof objectSchema> to get the type { property: string }.

```typescript
const objectSchema = v.object({

  property: v.string(),

});

type MyObject = Infer<typeof objectSchema>; // { property: string }
```

--------------------------------

### Using GenericMutationCtx in a Convex mutation

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/api/interfaces/server.GenericMutationCtx

Example from the GenericMutationCtx interface documentation. Shows how to use the mutation context (ctx) to insert documents, get user identity, and schedule functions. The mutation is transactional and atomic.

```typescript
import { mutation } from "./_generated/server";

import { internal } from "./_generated/api";

import { v } from "convex/values";



export const createTask = mutation({

  args: { text: v.string() },

  returns: v.id("tasks"),

  handler: async (ctx, args) => {

    // ctx.db: read and write documents

    const taskId = await ctx.db.insert("tasks", { text: args.text, completed: false });



    // ctx.auth: check the authenticated user

    const identity = await ctx.auth.getUserIdentity();



    // ctx.scheduler: schedule functions for later

    await ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, internal.notifications.send, { taskId });



    return taskId;

  },

});
```

### Set up ConvexProvider in src/main.ts

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/vue

Configure the Convex client in the Vue app entry point to make it available on every page. Uses the VITE_CONVEX_URL environment variable for the deployment URL.

```typescript
import { convexVue } from 'convex-vue'
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import App from './App.vue'

const app = createApp(App)

app.use(convexVue, {
  url: import.meta.env.VITE_CONVEX_URL,
})

app.mount('#app')
```

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/bun

Runs `bunx convex dev` to log in, create a project, and sync functions with the dev deployment. It also creates a `convex/` folder.

```bash
bunx convex dev
```

### Subscribe to a Convex query with useQuery in Svelte

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/svelte

Use `useQuery()` to subscribe to a Convex query. When the data changes on the server, the component updates. The example shows loading, error, and success states.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">  import { useQuery } from "convex-svelte";  import { api } from "../convex/_generated/api.js";  const messages = useQuery(api.messages.list, () => ({ searchWords: [] }));</script>{#if messages.isLoading}  Loading...{:else if messages.error != null}  failed to load: {messages.error.toString()}{:else}  <ul>    {#each messages.data as message}      <li>        <span>{message.author}</span>        <span>{message.body}</span>      </li>    {/each}  </ul>{/if}
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Auth0 provider with environment variables in auth.config.ts

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/auth/auth0

Use environment variables for Auth0 domain and application ID in the Convex auth configuration to support different tenants for development and production.

```ts
import { AuthConfig } from "convex/server";



export default {

  providers: [

    {

      domain: process.env.AUTH0_DOMAIN!,

      applicationID: process.env.AUTH0_CLIENT_ID!,

    },

  ],

} satisfies AuthConfig;
```

--------------------------------

### Register OpenTelemetry tracer provider and AI SDK integration

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/agents/debugging

Install @ai-sdk/otel, @opentelemetry/api, @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http, @opentelemetry/resources, and @opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base. This setup exports spans to an OTLP backend using environment variables for the endpoint and token.

```typescript
import { OpenTelemetry } from "@ai-sdk/otel";

import { trace } from "@opentelemetry/api";

import { OTLPTraceExporter } from "@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http";

import { resourceFromAttributes } from "@opentelemetry/resources";

import {

  BasicTracerProvider,

  SimpleSpanProcessor,

} from "@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base";

import { registerTelemetry } from "ai";



const tracerProvider = new BasicTracerProvider({

  resource: resourceFromAttributes({ "service.name": "convex-agent" }),

  spanProcessors: [

    new SimpleSpanProcessor(

      new OTLPTraceExporter({

        url: process.env.OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT,

        headers: {

          Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_TOKEN}`,

        },

      }),

    ),

  ],

});

trace.setGlobalTracerProvider(tracerProvider);

registerTelemetry(new OpenTelemetry());
```

--------------------------------

### Connect React app to Convex backend

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/react

In src/main.tsx, creates a ConvexReactClient and wraps the app with ConvexProvider. The client uses the VITE_CONVEX_URL environment variable.

```typescript
import React from "react";

import ReactDOM from "react-dom/client";

import App from "./App";

import "./index.css";

import { ConvexProvider, ConvexReactClient } from "convex/react";



const convex = new ConvexReactClient(import.meta.env.VITE_CONVEX_URL as string);



ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(

  <React.StrictMode>

    <ConvexProvider client={convex}>

      <App />

    </ConvexProvider>

  </React.StrictMode>,

);
```
